sasha: Heads-up — saw a latency regression on the GQA path for MQA models during canary. Short sequences (<=64) spike ~18-25% p99.

kevin: Ugh. Is this on paged-kv only or also contiguous layouts?

sasha: Primarily paged. Looks correlated with KV-page fragmentation after recent KV-striping change. When fragments are small we’re falling back to the generic attn kernel instead of the MQA-optimized path.

maria: Do we have a minimal repro? sample logs / perf numbers?

sasha: Attached snippets from the canary run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-12T18:02:12Z] model=mqa-7b variant=pagedkv block_size=32 seq=48 batch=8 kernel=attn_generic latency=12.2ms
[2026-03-12T18:02:12Z] model=mqa-7b variant=pagedkv block_size=32 seq=48 batch=8 kernel=attn_mqa_fast fallback=true latency=15.4ms
[2026-03-12T18:02:12Z] model=mqa-7b variant=contig block_size=32 seq=48 batch=8 kernel=attn_mqa_fast latency=11.9ms
```
Key bit: when KV pages are split across stripes we fail the layout check in kernel picker.

aj: That layout check was tightened for correctness after the thread-safety fix. Maybe too conservative now.

nora: From infra side: the new stripe allocator increased interleaving to improve utilization — but it creates more small fragments for short-lived sessions.

maria: So two vectors: allocator making fragments + stricter kernel acceptance rule. Either could explain fallback to generic kernel.

bench-bot: Quick microbench results (local repro):
```
> ./kv_bench --model mqa-7b --layout paged --block 32 --seq 48 --batch 8
attn_mqa_fast: enabled=false (layout_check_failed)
attn_generic: 11.9ms
attn_generic: 12.1ms
attn_generic: 12.0ms
```

sasha: Hypothesis: if we relax the alignment predicate to allow small cross-stripe adjacency (with metadata guard) we can keep mqa_fast enabled for most short seq cases. Also try smaller page block_size=16 for frag-heavy workloads.

kevin: Can we autotune: when seq<=64 prefer block_size=16 and use a fallback hysteresis so we don't flip-flop?

aj: We already have hysteresis but threshold is global. Need seqlen-aware hysteresis + layout score metric (frag_ratio).

maria: Proposal: 1) add frag_ratio metric on allocator, 2) kernel picker consults frag_ratio+seq to pick kernel and block_size, 3) autotune job that sweeps block_size in canary and measures p99 and token throughput.

sasha: I sketched a small scoring function this morning:
```
score = w_seq * exp(-seq/64) + w_frag * frag_ratio + w_hw * hw_type_score
if score < threshold: pick mqa_fast path else pick generic
```
We'd tune w_* via offline sweep.

nora: Infra can emit frag_ratio per host and we can feed that to the console. I'll add a metric.

bench-bot: Suggest parallel microbench sweep (cheap): {block_size: [16,24,32], seq: [32,48,64], frag_ratio: [0.1,0.3,0.6]} — I can run on a small fleet. ETA 2h.

kevin: Also add a short heatmap matrix to rollout dashboard so PMs can see impact vs cost.

aj: Implementation notes: kernel picker change is two parts: 1) expose frag_ratio in layout metadata, 2) path selector reads seq + frag_ratio and consults small lookup table (fast), not run expensive checks. Keep the legacy check as a final safety gate.

maria: Risk: relaxing the check could expose correctness edge-cases on very odd layouts — keep strict check in slow path and enable a debug flag to gather counterexamples.

sasha: Action items: 
- nora: emit frag_ratio metric + per-host histogram (priority).
- bench-bot: run microbench sweep and post heatmap (ETA 2h).
- aj: prototype seqlen-aware hysteresis + lookup table in kernel picker (PR target EOD).
- kevin: add UX heatmap on console (low-pri but useful).
- maria: run safety canary with relaxed predicate + debug logging (after PR).

nora: acked. will open infra ticket and patch exporter.

bench-bot: queued sweep job 3123456790 -> results will be posted to the thread.

kevin: If the sweep looks good we should bake an adaptive default: block_size=16 for seq<=64 on paged layouts. Saves latency and probably iso cost.

maria: Agree, but gate rollout behind canary and a regression guard that compares model quality and latency.

sasha: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the small PR and a short repro checklist. If anyone sees other regressions in canary please ping me directly. :thumbsup:
